questions.q: What is this capstone course's role in the AI Engineer path?
options: It teaches an entirely new topic not covered by earlier courses
It replaces the need for any earlier course in the path
It closes out the path by having you ship three real projects using what you already know
It only covers career preparation, with no project building
questions.explain: The course doesn't introduce new material — it's where everything from earlier courses in the path gets applied to ship three real, working systems end to end.

questions.q: What are the three flagship projects built in this course, in order?
options: A chatbot, a web scraper, and a mobile app
A production RAG knowledge assistant, an AI data analyst (SQL/APIs), and a tool-using agent with human approval
A blockchain app, an NFT marketplace, and a DAO
Three different versions of the same RAG assistant
questions.explain: The three flagship projects are the RAG knowledge assistant, the AI data analyst working with SQL and APIs, and the tool-using agent with human approval, security, and logging.

questions.q: Why does this course avoid building around one fictional company?
options: Because a capstone is meant to produce something that's actually the student's own, built under their own name
Fictional companies are against the catalog's content policy for all courses
Because fictional companies are too hard to write realistically
There is no stated reason in the lesson
questions.explain: The lesson states this is intentional: the student builds the project themselves, under their own name, in their own repository, rather than following a scripted fictional scenario.

questions.q: According to this lesson's portfolio strategy, what beats a GitHub profile with fifteen half-finished notebooks?
options: A profile with fifty half-finished notebooks instead of fifteen
A single notebook with no README at all
Nothing — more projects is always better regardless of completion
Two or three complete, measured, deployed AI projects with honest READMEs
questions.explain: The lesson argues depth over breadth: two or three genuinely complete, documented projects demonstrate finishing ability far better than many abandoned ones.

questions.q: Which of the following is NOT one of the four things this lesson says a "complete" project needs?
options: A real end-to-end pipeline that calls an actual LLM API
A measured evaluation with real numbers
A deployed, callable service
A guarantee from the student that the project will get them a job offer
questions.explain: The four completeness criteria are a real end-to-end pipeline, a measured evaluation, a deployed service, and a README stating architecture and tradeoffs — not any guarantee about job outcomes.
